Name: latent_answer_layerwise_depth
Title: How Deep Is the Answer? Layerwise Emergence and Difficulty-Adaptive Depth in Reasoning
Short Hypothesis: The final answer becomes linearly decodable at earlier layers for easy problems and later layers for hard ones, and this decode-depth is a mechanistic difficulty signal that can drive layer-wise early exit and depth-adaptive compute.
Related Work: Logit/tuned lens (Belrose 2023); Schuster et al. (2022) CALM early-exit; Din et al. (2023) jumping to conclusions. Prior early-exit uses output-confidence per token. We tie exit to the layerwise emergence depth of the reasoning answer and its correlation with problem difficulty, offering a depth-based compute policy for reasoning specifically.
Abstract: We study the depth at which reasoning models internally resolve their answers. Using tuned-lens decoding at the final CoT position, we measure the earliest layer at which the correct answer is linearly recoverable and hypothesize that this decode-depth scales with problem difficulty-shallow for easy items, deep for hard ones. We validate the signal against independent difficulty measures (solve rate, required steps) and test its stability across paraphrases. We then exploit it: a depth-adaptive policy exits the forward pass early when the answer is confidently decodable, saving layer compute on easy problems. We compare against per-token confidence early-exit and fixed-depth baselines on accuracy-versus-FLOPs. We also analyze the mechanism: which layers perform 'reasoning consolidation' and whether hard problems recruit additional late-layer computation absent in easy ones. Finally we ask whether depth and CoT-length efficiency are complementary (do easy problems that resolve shallowly also emit shorter traces?), integrating vertical (layer) and horizontal (token) views of efficient reasoning. The work provides a mechanistic difficulty gauge and a depth-adaptive inference method grounded in where, not just when, answers form.
Experiments: 1. Train tuned-lens per layer on R1-Distill; decode answer at final position across layers for GSM8K/MATH. 2. Define decode-depth = earliest layer with stable correct decode; correlate with solve-rate and step-count difficulty. 3. Paraphrase-robustness of decode-depth. 4. Depth-adaptive early exit: exit when lens-confidence at layer L exceeds threshold; sweep to accuracy vs mean layers/FLOPs. 5. Baselines: token-confidence exit, fixed truncated depth. 6. Analyze late-layer recruitment on hard items via per-layer contribution norms. 7. Correlate decode-depth with trace length for the horizontal/vertical integration.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Tuned-lens can be unfaithful to the true computation; early decode may reflect prior bias not reasoning. Depth-based exit requires custom inference support and may interact poorly with KV-cache/generation. Difficulty correlation may be weak or dataset-specific. Layer-skipping can degrade multi-token generation quality.
